chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
O son of Adam, whatever you earn beyond your basic needs, you are only a treasurer of it for others.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on wealth beyond basic needs?
ai.summary: In this famous aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) redefines ownership by distinguishing between basic sustenance (quoot) and surplus, framing the latter as a divine trust (amanah) for the community. This concept underpins the Shia jurisprudence of Zakat and Khums, where the wealthy act as custodians of resources that are ultimately due to the poor, emphasizing social justice over absolute private property rights.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 192. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
O son of Adam, whatever you earn beyond your basic needs you are only a treasurer of it for others.
